Rashi on Eruvin 100b:10:1.english: [Where one] is wearing shoes - It is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:10:2.hebrew: לא סיים מסאני - אסור, שעשבים נדבקין בקשרי אצבעותיו ונתלשין:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:10:2.english: [One who] is not wearing shoes - [It is] forbidden, as grasses stick to the joints of his toes and are uprooted.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:11:1.hebrew: עוקצא - אשפי"א, כפול מתחתיו, והעשבים נדבקים שם ותולשן:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:11:1.english: A spike - Espie [a nail], bent underneath, and the grass gets caught there and he uproots it.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:12:1.hebrew: שרכא - פתילה ארוכה. שהעשב ארוך — אסור:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:12:1.english: Sherakha - A long cord; [a case] where the grass is long is forbidden.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:13:1.hebrew: כר"ש - דאמר: דבר שאין מתכוין מותר:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:13:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Shimon - Who said: An unintentional act is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:14:1.english: To a matter of mitzvah - Marital relations.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:14:2.hebrew: ברגלים - לשון תשמיש, דכתיב (שופטים ה׳:כ״ז): ״בין רגליה כרע נפל שכב״:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:14:2.english: With [his] feet - An expression for conjugal relations, as it is written (Judges 5:27): “Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay.”

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:15:1.english: Also without knowledge - [This] is the beginning of that verse of “hastens with his feet.”

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:15:2.hebrew: נפש לא טוב - לא טובים הבנים הנעשים בלא דעת האשה, שהיה בעלה אץ ברגלים:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:15:2.english: [The] soul is not good - The children who are conceived without the woman’s consent, when her husband was hasty with his feet, are not good.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:16:1.english: One who has intercourse and repeats [it] - For he burdens her.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:17:1.hebrew: יבעול וישנה - שמחמת ביאה ראשונה נתאוה האשה והולבשה תאוה, וכשבא ביאה שניה היא מזרעת תחילה, והיכא דהיא מזרעת תחילה — יולדת זכר:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:17:1.english: He should have intercourse and repeat - For because of the first act of intercourse, the woman is aroused and enveloped in desire, and when he engages in a second act of intercourse, she emits seed first; and wherever she emits seed first, she gives birth to a male.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:17:2.english: With consent - [With the consent of] the woman.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:18:1.english: For a matter of mitzva - Marital relations.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:18:2.english: [Men of] understanding - Those who understand one matter from another.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:19:1.hebrew: יששכר - לאה תבעה את יעקב לדבר מצוה, ותאמר: ״אלי תבוא כי שכר שכרתיך וגו'״:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:19:1.english: Issachar - Leah demanded of Jacob for the conjugal mitzvah, and said: “You must come in to me, for indeed I have hired you...”

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:1:1.hebrew: דלא קא עביד איסורא - כשהוא יושב ואינו נותן, הלאו דבל תגרע והעשה דונתן על קרנות נעקרין מאליהן. אבל זה, ישיבתו תשמיש הוא — שהוא משתמש באילן:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:1:1.english: Where one does not commit a transgression - When he sits [passively] and does not place [the blood], the negative commandment of "Do not diminish" and the positive commandment of "And he shall place [it] upon the horns" are uprooted of their own accord. But [in the case of] this one, his sitting is [itself an act of] use, for he is making use of a tree.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:21:1.english: The pain of pregnancy - Pregnant women are ill.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:21:2.english: In accordance with its plain meaning - The pain of childbirth.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:22:2.hebrew: והוא ימשל בך - שהוא מושל לומר בפה תאות לבו, והאשה בלב, ובושה להוציא בפה:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:22:2.english: “And he shall rule over you” - That he has the mastery to express his heart’s desire verbally, whereas the woman [longs] in [her] heart, and is shy to express [it] verbally.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:22:3.english: That she makes herself pleasing before him - She displays expressions of affection before him.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:24:1.english: Wrapped like a mourner - [She is] ashamed to go out with her head uncovered.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:24:2.hebrew: מנודה לכל אדם - לקמיה מפרש, שאסורה לכל אדם חוץ מבעלה, והאיש נושא נשים הרבה:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:24:2.english: Ostracized from all people - [The Gemara] explains below that she is forbidden to all people except her husband, whereas a man may marry many women.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:24:3.english: And incarcerated within a prison - [As it is written:] “All glorious is the king’s daughter within” (Psalms 45:14) [as she is confined to the house].

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:26:2.hebrew: כבהמה - שכורעת כשהיא משתנת, ודרך פרידה לעשות כן:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:26:2.english: Like an animal - That she crouches when she urinates, and it is the way of a she-mule to do so.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:26:3.english: A pillow for her husband - That he is on top during marital relations.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:27:1.hebrew: שבח הוא לה - יושבת ומשתנת בצניעות, ואינה חסרה כלום בדבר. ונעשית כר לבעלה — אין לה טורח כל כך; טורחו מרובה משלה:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:27:1.english: [These are] praise for her - She sits and urinates modestly, and loses nothing by the matter. And [as for] "she serves as a pillow for her husband" — she does not have that much exertion; his exertion is greater than hers.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:28:2.english: By the beasts of the earth - In that He placed wisdom in them to instruct us.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:28:3.hebrew: שמפייס - הולך ופושט כנפיו, והוא פיוס, כדאמר לקמן שאומר לה לקנות מלבוש שמגיע לארץ:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:28:3.english: Which cajoles - He walks and spreads his wings, and this is [his] cajoling, as [the Gemara] says below, that he says to her [that he will] buy [her] a garment that reaches to the ground.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:29:1.hebrew: צניעות מחתול - שאינו מטיל רעי בפני אדם, ומכסה צואתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:29:1.english: Modesty from a cat - For it does not defecate in front of people, and it covers its excrement.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:29:2.hebrew: וגזל מנמלה - דכתיב (משלי ו׳:ח׳) (אגרה) בקיץ לחמה, ואין אחת גוזלת מאכל חברתה:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:29:2.english: And stealing from the ant - As it is written (Proverbs 6:8): “[She gathers] her bread in the summer,” and not one [ant] steals the food of another.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:29:3.english: And forbidden relations from the dove - For it does not mate except with its partner.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:2:1.hebrew: יבש - שאין בו לחלוח, ולאו מחובר הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:2:1.english: A dry [tree] - In which there is no moisture, and it is not [considered] attached [to the ground].

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:30:1.english: A coat - A garment that they call in Old French cote:

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:30:2.hebrew: לבתר הכי - לאחר בעילה, שמנענע וכופף ראשו לה לארץ:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:30:2.english: After this - After mating, when it nods and bows its head toward her to the ground.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:30:3.english: If he has - [The means] with which to buy [it].

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:4:1.hebrew: בימות החמה - יבש מותר, דליכא אפי' משום מראית העין, שהרי ניכר לכל שהוא יבש, שאינו מוציא עלין. והא דקתני אסור — בימות הגשמים, שאין ניכר בין לח בין יבש, ואיכא משום מראית העין:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:4:1.english: In the summer - A dry [tree] is permitted, for there is not even [a concern] of the appearance of impropriety, as it is evident to all that it is dry, since it does not produce leaves. And that which was taught, [that it is] forbidden — [that is] in the rainy season, when it is not discernible between a green [tree] and a dry [one], and there is [a concern] of the appearance of impropriety.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:5:1.hebrew: קא נתרי פירי - שנשארו בו משנה שעברה, ואתי למשרי ביה תלישה דלח. נהי דעליה דיבש אטו עליה דלח לא גזרי', דהיא גופא גזירה — מיהו תלישה אטו תלישה נגזר:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:5:1.english: Fruit will fall off - [Fruit] that remained on it from the previous year, and [people] will come to permit thereby detaching [from] a moist [tree]. Granted that climbing a dry [tree] on account of climbing a moist [tree] we do not decree, as that is itself a decree; however, detaching on account of detaching we should decree!

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:6:1.english: In [the case of] a gaduda - A shoot whose branches have all fallen off.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:6:2.hebrew: בקעה מצא - כלומר, אינן בני תורה שידעו להזהר, כבקעה זו שאין לה שומר, והכל פרוץ:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:6:2.english: [Rav] found a valley - That is to say, they are not Torah scholars who would know how to be careful, like this valley that has no watchman and everything is breached.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:7:1.hebrew: ואץ ברגלים חוטא - אלמא הלוך נמי חטא קרי ליה, והכא איכא חטא — שתולש עשבים:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:7:1.english: And he who hastens with his feet sins - Evidently, [the verse] calls walking, too, a sin; and here there is a sin — that he uproots grass.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:8:1.hebrew: לחים - אסור, דהוי תולש; יבשין — כתלושין דמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:8:1.english: Green [grass] - [It is] prohibited, as it constitutes uprooting; dry [grass] is considered as [already] detached.

Rashi on Eruvin 100b:9:1.hebrew: בימות החמה - זרע יש בגבעולין, ומשירן:
Rashi on Eruvin 100b:9:1.english: In the summer - There is seed in the stalks, and he dislodges them.

Tosafot on Eruvin 100b:13:1.hebrew: והאידנא דקי"ל כר"ש כולהו שרי - פי' ר"ח, דהאי היתר לא קאי אלא אעשבים, דשרי בכל ענין. אבל באילן, אין להוכיח שם שום היתר, אפילו יבש — דשייך למיגזר טפי, משום דמנכרא מילתא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 100b:13:1.english: "And now that we maintain in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, all of them are permitted" - Rabbeinu Chananel explained that this permission applies only to grass, which is permitted in any manner. But regarding a tree, one cannot deduce any permission from there, even [for] a dry one, as it is more applicable to decree [a prohibition], because the matter is conspicuous.

Tosafot on Eruvin 100b:8:1.hebrew: לא קשיא הא בלחים הא ביבשים - וא"ת: והא לעיל אסרינן ביבש, דפריך: "והא נתרי קינסי כו'"? וי"ל: דבאילן שהוא גבוה שייך למגזר טפי, משום דמינכר ביה ניתרי קינסי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 100b:8:1.english: This is not difficult: This is with green [grass], that is with dry [grass] - And if you say: But earlier we prohibited [climbing] in [the case of] a dry [tree], as [the Gemara] challenged: "Yet twigs fall off, etc."? And one can say: With a tree, which is tall, it is more applicable to decree [a prohibition], because the falling off of twigs is noticeable on it.
